title: Get started
description: Three ways in: play in your browser, run it on a Teensy, or build hardware.

config.title: Three ways *in*.
config.subtitle: Play in your browser, run it on a Teensy, or build hardware. The step-by-step documentation lives in the MusicBrain repository on GitHub; guides marked (NL) are in Dutch.

items.title: Play in your browser
items.markdown:
1. Open the [editor](https://editor.musicbrain.nl/) and select **Modular MB**.
2. Load a ready-made patch from **Solo** or **Poly**.
3. Open **Simulation**, start audio at a low volume and play the on-screen keyboard or a MIDI keyboard.
4. Export the project as JSON — browser storage is not a backup.

[Step by step →](https://github.com/MarkWestbroek/MusicBrain#try-it-in-the-browser)

items.title: Use a Teensy
items.markdown:
You need a **Teensy 4.1**, a USB data cable and a computer; sampler and bank patches also need PSRAM and a microSD card.

1. Download a [released firmware](https://github.com/MarkWestbroek/MusicBrain/releases) and flash it with PJRC Teensy Loader.
2. Connect from the editor's Teensy link and check the version it reports.
3. Listen over USB audio — the current firmware has no standalone analog output.

[Use a Teensy →](https://github.com/MarkWestbroek/MusicBrain#use-a-teensy) · [Firmware distribution (NL)](https://github.com/MarkWestbroek/MusicBrain/blob/main/doc/firmware-distributie.md) · [Teensy on a PC (NL)](https://github.com/MarkWestbroek/MusicBrain/blob/main/doc/teensy-aan-de-pc.md)

items.title: Build hardware
items.markdown:
Stick to one board generation. Check each card's revision, pinouts, BOM/fab files and validation status, and verify power and orientation before first power-up.

A clean ERC/DRC or fab package is not proof of an assembled, tested board.

[Build hardware →](https://github.com/MarkWestbroek/MusicBrain#build-hardware)

config.title: Before you start
config.markdown:
- **Browser:** a current Chrome or Edge gives the most straightforward Web MIDI/USB workflow. Audio, MIDI and serial access each ask for permission.
- **Backup:** export your projects as JSON; browser storage is not a backup.
- **Teensy:** Teensy 4.1 and a USB data cable; PSRAM and microSD for samplers and banks. The documented flashing and audio workflow is for Windows.
- **Optional:** AI assistance and local speech generation have their own configuration. The core editor needs neither.

Only the combinations above are documented; others may work but have not been tested.
